mutant.description: The strongest control here is that the read-back instrument is RELEASE-SPECIFIC and the two existing ones are live mutants of it. ap6_verify.py asserts one tool ADDED and a DIFFERENT env key added; ap7_verify.py asserts .env key names UNCHANGED and ROUTES +3. Run against this correct deploy BOTH would FAIL -- ap6 on its tool limb, ap7 on both its env and route limbs -- so a passing verdict here cannot have come from a verifier that would pass anything. Second control, on the base: before the deploy the host's md5 mismatches against the RELEASE list were required to EQUAL the base-vs-release differ set exactly (3 files), which fails if the host were running anything other than the base; it read yes. Third: the bad-extension arm was handed a graph_call that RAISES if reached, so a refusal occurring AFTER a fetch would have surfaced as AssertionError rather than SiteToS3Refused.
mutant.expected: Running ap6_verify.py or ap7_verify.py against this deploy FAILS -- ap6 on its tool limb (it asserts one tool ADDED; this release adds none) and ap7 on both its env limb (it asserts .env names UNCHANGED; this release adds exactly one) and its route limb (it asserts ROUTES +3; this release adds none). The before-state md5 control was expected to show the host's 3 mismatches EQUAL to the base-vs-release differ set, and the bad-extension arm was expected to raise SiteToS3Refused rather than AssertionError.
mutant.observed: Each inherited verifier's assertions are contradicted by this release's measured deltas: tools 67 -> 67 (ap6 would fail), .env names 53 -> 54 (ap7 would fail), routes 56 -> 56 (ap7 would fail). The before-state control read 'host is running the BASE: mismatches equal the base-vs-release differ set (3): yes'. The bad-extension arm raised SiteToS3Refused and the injected graph_call was never reached, so entry_docx_reached_network is false.

determinism.description: AC1 and AC2 are deterministic reads of committed state and live AWS configuration. AC1 was run across a moving HEAD (0ae447fd80 -> eda546e5ad) and returned the same verdict; the served read was run twice, once with a defective fee predicate and once corrected, and every field other than the one under repair was identical across both runs.
determinism.method: Two same-input runs compared per instrument: AC1 was run across a moving box/sitez HEAD (0ae447fd80 -> eda546e5ad) with the three HEAD-equality files re-verified immediately before the recorded run; ap10_served.py was run twice, once with a defective fee predicate and once corrected; ap10_verify.py's before and after are the two halves of one paired read.
determinism.observed: AC1 returned the same verdict on both runs despite HEAD moving, because the three files it compares were untouched by the intervening commits. Across the two served runs every field other than the one under repair was identical: tool_takes_extension, market_update_root_equals_address, bad_extension_refused and objects_written read the same both times, and only fee_root_unchanged moved, from false to true, when its predicate was corrected.
